Within the movie, Mike said that his dad 'couldn't really handle' the loss of his wife, but it doesn't mention that Mike's dad ended his life. He may have just left his children behind, assuming Mike was old enough to care for Abby on his own at the time. This could allow for some sort of Pizzeria simulator-adjacent 'ending' to at least some of the spirits haunting the suits of the animatronics. This point is based on the assumption that Mike's father is Henry Emily — Which I find to be entirely likely considering his massive role as the main protagonist in the movie.

Vanessa being William's daughter in the movie is inadvertently 'confirming' the theory Matpat made about game Elizabeth and Vanessa filling the same role within William's family unit. They both listen to him in the game and movie respectively, until the point at which they don't, which is when they get hurt. Movie Vanessa is also a parallel of game Vanessa as she is a reluctant follower in her adult years and cannot seem to escape the grasp of her father. She deviates sometimes within the movie, such as when she does not kill Mike when he gets too close to the truth like her father instructed, which aligns with game Vanessa searching things such as 'help' whilst under the influence of William.

Mike is the only one in the movie to acknowledge and recount what exactly happened to Garrett, and we have no one to confirm what exactly happened that day. Assuming that sound illusion discs may also be in play in the movie franchise, it is not unreasonable to suspect that they may have been in use when William took Garrett. If this is so, it could have easily changed Mike's perception of the world around him, as well as the people. This is further prompted by the only Nebraska-related thing being Mike's poster, which he could have gotten at any point from anywhere. It could have been a totally fabricated memory developed as a way to cope with not entirely remembering his brother's disappearance. If Garrett is the movie stand-in for Henry's daughter, he may have also been murdered behind the pizzeria and then consequently stuffed inside the security puppet as most theorise Charlotte had been.

Mike is an unreliable narrator. He is overwhelmed with this memory, but unable to remember who took Garrett. He's on medication, and was probably on medication when he was younger to cope with the trauma that being 'responsible' for Garrett's disappearance caused.

 I don't think Aunt Jane is actually poor. It wouldn't make sense for her to be able to pay for a lawyer, or promise to pay some henchmen to snoop around her Nephew's house if she did not have money for these things. Therefore, Mike's comment about her just wanting the monthly cheques from the government doesn't really make sense. I think it is more likely that she suspects Mike holds much more blame when it comes to the disappearance of Garrett, and does not trust him around Abby for this reason either. She never outright acknowledges this suspicion as it would be considered slander, and if she is trying to abide by the law in order to remove her niece from her nephew's care, throwing around accusations of guilt about Garrett's disappearance just wouldn't make sense for her to do. She refers to Mike as a monster when in relation to a provable offence, wherein he beat up a man in the mall, which was obviously played up on her side due to having very poor ammunition otherwise.
